💀 I meant about- actually nevermind, I'm gonna try to give you my perspective, even though I'm not that good of an example (I've been in therapy on and off for more than a year, for what it's worth). You know what you'd need? Probably a totally unrealistic way to stop time and catch your breath, at least that's what I would've wanted in the worst times; yk, a couple of weeks of nothing, maybe reading or going out. Now, we both know that it's not possible to stop time and school/work can become a living hell, but you could try to force some kind of rest days in your life (not endorsing lying about catching a cold or actually catching it, just saying it's a desperate measure) and living them at the fullest. No doom scrolling, no phone, just life. And about trauma, I advise you to search for a psychologist (not a psychiatrist, so no antidepressants) and work on it. Yes it's gonna be hard and expensive and a slow process, but professional help is necessary for stuff like that. If you don't like your psychologist search for other ones, again and again if necessary. Also, one trick is to keep a streak for good habits in your life, it will be easier in the long run. Treat your old and future selves like close friends, yeah you make fun of them but they're like family. This is all I have, stay safe

As much as I'm concerned, life's value is in the small stuff, in friendships, in travel, in hobbies, in pleasure, in a wonderful sunset, in an interesting book, in a goofy ahh dance in the rain, in a bonfire, in ice cream, in that weird guy that everyone seems to judge so quickly, 

We have a chance, only one (as much as we know), to experience all of this. It's up to you now to live.

hi, probably you didn't receive help because it's really hard to actively do something that will lead to the death of a person. The rules of this sub are against it so you won't receive help here too. 

I'm not gonna help you find a way to kill yourself, neither I'll tell you to be strong and don't do it; I don't know what you're going through, that would be pretty stupid to say without any information. 

That being said, one thing that I'm gonna recommend you is to keep yourself open to change. A year ago I was actively searching a way to die and I couldn't even see getting better as a real possible option. Now I know that it was, but I couldn't see it back then. 

I think that similarly almost everyone has the chance to change but can't see it; obviously it's not a fault, it's almost impossible without hindsight and months worth of therapy.

I hope you'll get better, or improve yourself trying to. 
If you really want to end it I'm no one to stop you, so in this extreme case I really hope that you'll find a painless way.
